verses.english: Linked Discourses 45.11
2. Meditation
Meditation (1st)
At Sāvatthī.
“Mendicants, I wish to go on retreat for a fortnight.

verses.pali: Namhi kenaci upasaṅkamitabbo, aññatra ekena piṇḍapātanīhārakenā”ti.
verses.english: No-one should approach me, except for the one who brings my almsfood.”

verses.pali: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paṭissutvā nāssudha koci bhagavantaṁ upasaṅkamati, aññatra ekena piṇḍapātanīhārakena.
verses.english: “Yes, sir,” replied those mendicants. And no-one approached him, except for the one who brought the almsfood.

verses.pali: Atha kho bhagavā tassa aḍḍhamāsassa accayena paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito bhikkhū āmantesi:
verses.english: Then after a fortnight had passed, the Buddha came out of retreat and addressed the mendicants:

verses.pali: “yena svāhaṁ, bhikkhave, vihārena paṭhamābhisambuddho viharāmi, tassa padesena vihāsiṁ.
verses.english: “Mendicants, I’ve been practicing part of the meditation I practiced when I was first awakened.
I understand that
there’s feeling conditioned by wrong view
and feeling conditioned by right view. …
There’s feeling conditioned by wrong immersion,
and feeling conditioned by right immersion.
There’s feeling conditioned by desire.
There’s feeling conditioned by thought.
There’s feeling conditioned by perception.

verses.pali: chando ca avūpasanto hoti, vitakko ca avūpasanto hoti, saññā ca avūpasantā hoti, tappaccayāpi vedayitaṁ;
verses.english: As long as desire, thought, and perception are not stilled, there is feeling conditioned by that.

verses.pali: chando ca vūpasanto hoti, vitakko ca vūpasanto hoti, saññā ca vūpasantā hoti, tappaccayāpi vedayitaṁ;
verses.english: When desire, thought, and perception are stilled, there is feeling conditioned by that.

verses.pali: appattassa pattiyā atthi āyāmaṁ, tasmimpi ṭhāne anuppatte tappaccayāpi vedayitan’”ti.
verses.english: There is effort to attain the unattained. When that state has been attained, there is also feeling conditioned by that.”
